subject: Model fit follow-up & Redwood-verified benchmarks for Acme (next steps)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit follow-up & Redwood-verified benchmarks for Acme (next steps)

Hi Lisa — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of call:
- Goal: evaluate viable LLM serving options for Acme's customer support summarization pipeline (95–200 token outputs, ~1.2M monthly requests).
- Key constraints: P50 latency target <= 120ms, cost sensitivity (aim to reduce token spend vs current setup), and data residency for EU traffic (we flagged private deployment).

Redwood recommendations (initial):
1) rw-7B-lite (quantized) — baseline: best price/latency balance for majority of queries. Redwood-verified perf: p50=42ms p95=125ms, sustained TPS ~55 on dedicated g4dn pool.
2) rw-13B-qa (int8) — higher quality for long-context answers; perf: p50=78ms p95=220ms, TPS ~22.
3) rw-34B-cmp (fp16) — fallback for high-importance tickets where quality is paramount. Perf: p50=210ms p95=480ms.

Benchmarks & artifacts (shared):
- Redwood-verified performance profile: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/acme-benchmark-487 (includes TPS by model, latency percentiles, and memory/cost estimates).
- Prompt sets and eval harness (sample test set we ran): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmePromptSets
- Attached: acme_benchmark_results_q1.pdf (high level summary + charts).

Quality/regression note:
- We observed a ~3% drop in ROUGE-L for rw-7B-lite on one of your long-tail prompt clusters vs the 13B baseline. That likely indicates a prompt-engineering/temperature tuning opportunity rather than a model bug, but we'll surface candidate prompt edits in the next run.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm which 2 model variants you'd like us to include in the POC (suggest rw-7B-lite + rw-13B-qa).
2) Share a >500-sample labeled subset (or allow us to sample from your staging logs) so we can run targeted evals and prompt tuning against your prompt clusters.
3) Quick sync next week to review tuned prompts, cost estimates, and an MVP rollout plan (approx 2–3 week POC).

Can you confirm availability for a 30-min review on Tue/Wed next week? Also please confirm whether we should run evals on EU data (we can run in-region private infra).

Thanks — happy to jump back on a call to walk through the dashboard.

— Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: acme_benchmark_results_q1.pdf
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmecorp.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: dp@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit follow-up & Redwood-verified benchmarks for Acme (next steps)

Alex — thanks for the detailed recap and the dashboard link. Quick answers: 
- Confirm we want rw-7B-lite + rw-13B-qa in the POC. Cost is a key factor; try to bias tuning toward the 7B where possible.
- We can share a 800-sample labeled set (sanitized) by EOD tomorrow; EU subset is required (about 20% of samples).

A couple of follow-ups: 
1) The ~3% ROUGE-L regression you mentioned — can you include a short list of the specific prompt clusters where that showed up? We want to understand risk to NPS/CSAT.
2) Any guidance on tokenization differences between rw-7B-lite and our current hosted model? We noticed earlier there were small truncation differences at the 200-token boundary.

Would prefer Wed 03/25 10:00am PT for the review.

Thanks,
Lisa
Head of Data Platform | Acme Corp
lisa.chen@acmecorp.com

Thanks Alex — looping in a couple of notes from the evals team.

- Prompt clusters where we saw the ROUGE-L dip: "long-agent-summary" and "multi-ticket-merge" (examples included in the Drive folder under /examples). For those clusters the 7B tends to drop some connective phrasing; weve attached an experimental prompt set that recovers ~2.1% on average (prompt_sets_acme_v2.jsonl).
- Tokenization: rw-series uses SentencePiece with a ~50k unigram vocab; compared to the hosted model you mentioned there are small differences at truncation boundaries. We'll include a tokenization report in the next artifact set so you can see exact token counts for the 800-sample set.

If we get the 800-sample labeled set, we can do:
A) A targeted eval run (24–36 hours) across both model variants with the prompt tuning applied.
B) A cost projection for steady-state after tuning with expected TPS and per-token cost breakdowns.

I uploaded the prompt set and a short readme to the Drive folder.

— Marissa Cole
